{{Short description|Australian-Swedish chemist and educator}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}}
{{Use Australian English|date=November 2019}}

'''Ian Alan Nicholls''' (born 24 October 1962 in [[Melbourne]], Australia) is an educator and researcher in the fields of chemistry and chemical engineering and an academic leader. Since 2013 he has held the position of Dean of the Faculty of Health and Life Sciences at [[Linnaeus University]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Ian Nicholls |url=https://lnu.se/en/staff/ian.nicholls/ |accessdate=8 January 2020}}</ref> Sweden, and is a Deputy Vice Chancellor of the university.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lnu.se/employee/ian.nicholls?l=en|title=Ian Nicholls - Linnaeus University, Sweden - Lnu.se|work=lnu.se|access-date=6 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180430182814/https://lnu.se/employee/ian.nicholls?l=en|archive-date=30 April 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Education ==

After graduating from [[Penleigh and Essendon Grammar School]] (1980) he studied at the [[University of Melbourne]] (BSc(hons) and PhD in medicinal chemistry, 1981-1989). In 1998 he was awarded the title ''docent'' (habilitation/associate professor) by the Faculty of Engineering, [[Lund University]], Sweden.

== Career ==

A year (1989) as lecturer at [[Victoria University of Technology]] (then Western Institute) was followed by a move in 1989 to [[Cambridge University]] (UK) for a position as post-doctoral research fellow with Prof. [[Dudley H. Williams]] FRS, then in 1992 to [[Lund University]] (Sweden) with Prof. [[Klaus Mosbach]]. Over the years 1994 to 1999 he held a series of positions at Lund University and the [[University of Kalmar]] (from 2010 Linnaeus University) before being appointed as full professor of bioorganic chemistry in 2000. From 2007 until 2012 he was Head (''prefekt'') of the School of Natural Sciences, and as of 2013 Dean and Deputy Vice Chancellor. Since 2010 Nicholls has held a visiting professorship at [[Uppsala University]] (Sweden) and in 2014 he was appointed adjunct professor in Materials Science and Engineering at [[Jiangsu University]] (PRC).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://katalog.uu.se/empinfo?id=N10-186_3&q=nicholls|title=Ian A Nicholls|work=uu.se|access-date=6 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150707030707/http://katalog.uu.se/empinfo?id=N10-186_3&q=nicholls|archive-date=7 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research ==

Nicholls' research is primarily focused on the development of biomimetic materials and their application in sensing, catalysis and as biomaterials/therapeutics, and on fundamental studies of molecular recognition phenomena.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lnu.se/research-groups/bioorganic-and-biophysical-chemistry-laboratory?l=en|title=Bioorganic and Biophysical Chemistry Laboratory - Linnaeus University, Sweden - Lnu.se|work=lnu.se|access-date=6 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141023051121/http://lnu.se/research-groups/bioorganic-and-biophysical-chemistry-laboratory?l=en|archive-date=23 October 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> This is reflected in his work with [[molecular imprinting]] and concerning the anticoagulant [[warfarin]].<ref>Karlsson BC, Rosengren AM, Andersson PO, Nicholls IA (September 2007). "The spectrophysics of warfarin: implications for protein binding". J Phys Chem B 111 (35): 10520–8. [http://doi:10.1021/jp072505i doi:10.1021/jp072505i]{{dead link|date=November 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. {{PMID|17691835}}.</ref> He has a number of editorial responsibilities, including editor-in-chief for [[International Journal of Molecular Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mdpi.com/journal/ijms/editors/|title=IJMS|work=mdpi.com}}</ref>
